title: RAID EVENTS END FOR PLAYER 2 WHEN THE HOST LEAVES
why: In a career co-op raid, when the host extracts or dies while player 2 is still up, the host window spectates and keeps sending the world word, but with no raid flow in it (flowNetOut returns null once the raid is over for the host). Player 2 window only ends an event when a host word says so, and only reads the flow when it is there, so a live event stayed on for good: a coolant rupture kept his sight at 45 percent and the cold fog on him for the rest of the raid. Proven in a staged career pair: after 120 seconds the rupture was still live on player 2 with sight 0.45. Now the first spectating host word ends every live or warned event on player 2 window (it fades out as a normal end does), and no later host flow word is taken that raid, so a late word cannot bring it back. A live host that has no raid flow (a raid with no events) also sends null, but player 2 window has then never taken flow, so nothing happens there.
now: If your host extracts or goes down while a coolant rupture or another raid event is on, it now ends for you instead of leaving the fog on you for the rest of the raid.

edits.replacement: try{ if(m.fl) flowNetTake(m.fl); else if(m.fl===null&&flowPeer()) flowHostOff(); }catch(_fnt){}   // v16.xx (cloud-coop-host-out-events-end), CLOUD HUNT 2026-10-15: a spectating host (extracted or dead) sends fl null, so its live raid events end here too instead of staying on for good
